Results.ReviewText: After using a gas grill for a couple of years I missed the flavor and versatility of a charcoal grill.  My birthday was fast approaching and my wife asked me what I would like for the occasion.  She talked about a couple of things that I had mentioned would be nice to have, but finally I said that I wanted to get back to grilling with charcoal and suggested a Weber Kettle.  So that's what she got me, and I couldn't be happier.  I use it 3 - 4 times a week and it's a success every time.  (I'm thinking I may have to put my gas grill in mothballs).  Whether I grill direct or indirect that flavor is always there.  I have not ventured into smoking anything, but plan on going there soon.  The bottom line is that I love my Weber Kettle.

Results.ReviewText:
I bought a small Weber Kettle in 1991, and used it for about a year, until I backed over it with my car!  That Christmas, my dad bought me a Weber Original Kettle to replace the one I killed. He said he bought me the big one, so I could see it better behind the car!

 Since 1992, I used that Kettle to cook everything, including burgers, steaks, hot dogs, fish, vegetables, and briskets.  I loved that Kettle so much, in 2007, I bought a small Kettle to take to the beach, picnics, and camping trips. 

  The Kettle my dad gave me finally rusted through in 2018, but had always been stored outside, uncovered, in rain, snow, hail, sleet, cold, and blistering heat. It had been blown over in strong winds so many times, I have lost count.  The small Kettle I bought in 2007, still has the original grates and looks brand new. 

Today, my daughter’s boyfriend surprised me with a new 22” Original Kettle, to replace the old one I had had for over 25 years. I’m 50 now, and as well as these Weber Kettles are built, I expect this one to last well beyond my grilling days!!
Results.Title: Love my Weber Kettle!

Results.ReviewText:
Why Weber over a kettle at half the price?
Because parts are readily available locally.  Generic brands are tossed after rusted grates and legs fail.  I'd rather buy parts than a new grill every however often. 

Why the basic over the premium?

Wasn't worried about a large ash catcher, I have no issue with the ash pan.  Didn't need a lid thermometer since those aren't accurate. I know how to arrange charcoal for zones, so didn't need separators.  I have mitts so didn't need a top grate with hinges.

Wheels and legs seem a little weak and lid isn't air tight. For about $110, as long as the lid and kettle don't rust and grates are easy to find locally, I'm satisfied.

Its ultra-durable, porcelain-enameled lid and bowl retain heat, while the dampers easily adjust for precise temperature control.
